2021 – 22
May 2021 – Sep 2022  ·  St. Louis Park, MN

Software Engineer, Mobile

The Jed Mahonis Group

Built client Android applications in Kotlin and Java across more than three apps: authentication, API integration, Google Maps, and the interfaces on top of them.

The one I still point to is Little Free Library. I built the Android version of their app — the Google Maps integration for finding a library near you, the authentication flow, profile pictures and user information, and several of the screens around them. It went out to a global network of readers.

Before all of it: a high-school Java class in 2018, then the discovery that I could put things on the App Store. That is genuinely where this starts.

2025
Jul 2025 – May 2026  ·  Minnetonka, MN

AI Engineer

UnitedHealthcare

Architected an enterprise AI observability platform covering both legacy and cloud-native applications, preventing over $1M in annual losses by cutting mean time to recovery on systems where downtime is valued at $600K per minute.

Built custom pipeline tooling and MCP servers that let autonomous agents map complex system dependencies, plus agent-driven data retrieval that made member information reachable in natural language rather than through a query someone had to write.

UnitedHealthcare

Picked as one of 15 engineers out of UnitedHealth Group Technology’s 13,000 to start the company’s forward deployed engineering practice — embedded with business units rather than sitting on a platform team.

2026 – present  ·  Self-employed

Founder &
Principal Consultant

Vantix Strategies

A forward deployed engineering firm built on the belief that the value of AI shows up in production rather than in a proof of concept. We embed as an extension of a client’s engineering org, work through rapid development from kickoff to deployment, and hand over the full IP to the client.

The work spans AI orchestration — RAG, agents, LLM ops — embedded data engineering, and post-acquisition tech-stack consolidation. Founded in January 2026, and what I do full time since August.

Built
Selected  ·  2020 – 2026

Projects I have built over the years

2026  ·  TYPESCRIPT · POSTGRES · GEMINI

Luup

A SaaS platform that finds the people worth knowing in a network you already have — matching on alumni, past employers and location, with AI-drafted outreach and a discovery feed.

2025  ·  PYTHON · CV · OCR

Py-Doc

Document-layout computer vision, published on PyPI. A detection CNN trained on IBM’s PubLayNet parses page structure, then Tesseract reads region by region rather than treating a page as one flat block.

2023  ·  PYTORCH · YOLOV7

TikTok Watermark Remover

A YOLOv7 detector tracks a watermark that drifts around the frame, then inpainting reconstructs what was behind it. The hard part was training data: enough backgrounds that it learned the mark, not the video.

2021  ·  FLASK · PYTHON

COVID-19 Information Provider

Republished current figures during the stretch when official dashboards were slow and unreadable. Won the Congressional App Challenge for Minnesota’s 3rd district.

Also: two apps on the App Store before university — a 3D SceneKit game with Game Center leaderboards, and a SwiftUI app for my own high school — and a genetic algorithm that learned to play Flappy Bird, written up as a short paper.

Fig. 12
Seasons
The rest of the year

There is a sport for every season here

Running is the constant, but it is far from the only thing. I am at my best when the calendar is full, and Minnesota gives you a genuine reason to look forward to every season.

Winter

  • Nordic skiing — three American Birkebeiners so far, and the reason a Minnesota December is something to look forward to

Spring – Fall

  • Hiking and camping, usually with a tent at the end of it and a view worth the walk

Summer

  • Pickleball — pure fun, good company, and some of the best evenings of the year

All year

  • Lifting — the base everything else is built on, and what keeps the long days feeling good
